display.processing: Each band is calibrated to MJy/sr and divided by its own measured range, so hue shows where a band is bright relative to itself, not physical band ratios. One common minimum is subtracted; one asinh curve maps the mean of the bands and scales every band by the same factor. Pixels brighter than the display are scaled down as a whole, then quantized once to 8 bits. This does not reconstruct natural color.

models.nircam-six-filters: Fitted ring, in colour from 6 bands. Each mosaic is read about the star through its own WCS onto a sky plane in astronomical units; the star's position is the observation's target position (TARG_RA, TARG_DEC). Each band's background, the median in the 5–8″ annulus, is subtracted, and the band is divided by the 99.9th percentile of its own drawn samples, the sky-band composite's rule. The ring is measured on the mean of the bands: its ridge, the radius of peak brightness in each azimuth under nine binnings, traces an ellipse of semi-major axis 80.9 au, axis ratio 0.875 (inclination 29.0°), line of nodes at position angle 100.6°, centre 1.4 au from the star; the single binnings scatter by 0.1 au, 0.1° and 0.4°. This stands against Gáspár et al. (2026), arXiv:2608.27437's 80 au, 28.54° and 100.39°. Depth is not the image pushed backwards: an inclined ring of that geometry with gaussian radial width 22.7 au projects to the mean image with a residual of 1.04e-1 against a signal of 4.85e-1, where a spherical shell leaves 1.27e-1 and constant depth, what an extrusion assumes, leaves 2.18e-1. The ring's vertical height is a stated 0.05 of its radius (the projection changes by 0.4% across the heights tried), and which side is nearer is a convention: the south-south-west end of the minor axis is drawn nearer; this image does not say which end is. Colour: red F335M + F444W, green F250M + F300M, blue F182M + F210M, each channel the mean of its normalised bands, through the shared Lupton et al. (2004) asinh display (minimum 0, stretch 0.1, softening 8), which scales every channel of a pixel by the same factor so its hue survives. Each sky column's three channels are spread along the ring with one depth profile and normalised so the column reproduces its displayed colour. The image is drawn from 48 au, outside the coronagraph mask, to the grid edge with a taper from 120 au.

limitations: One epoch: no third axis was observed. The depth is the ring that best projects to the images, an inference from that projection, not a measurement.
Which side of the inclined ring is nearer the observer is a stated convention; the images alone cannot tell.
The ring’s vertical thickness is a stated convention; at this inclination the projection barely changes with it.
Azimuthal brightness differences in the images, from forward scattering and from real structure, are kept as measured; the ring model supplies only the depth.
Inside the coronagraph mask the star and its immediate surroundings are not data and are not drawn; the star is the host body’s own sphere.

Hue shows where each group of bands is bright relative to its own range, not physical band ratios: every band is divided by its own peak, as sky-band composites are. Colour differences across the ring are real differences in how the bands vary with position, not a measured colour of the dust.
Nothing finer than the mosaics’ pixels or the grid’s cells is in the drawn volume.
